subject.title: Talk: add context-aware durable voice sessions

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the full durable Talk session, cached-context, confirmation, summary, protocol, and configuration surface in one release, or stage the work behind a smaller canonical session foundation?
rationale: The patch introduces permanent cross-client protocol and operator configuration contracts, and repository evidence cannot determine whether maintainers want the full combined product surface or a narrower staged design.

options.title: Stage the foundation
options.body: First land a session-isolated durable ledger and reliable transcript lifecycle with real client proof, then review context packs and policy configuration separately.

options.title: Sponsor the full surface
options.body: Approve the combined product direction, require the isolation and transcript fixes, align the shared policy contract, and obtain Browser and iPhone proof before merge.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Keep current Talk behavior unchanged until the desired voice-session UX and permanent configuration contract are specified by an owner.

recommendation.title: Stage the foundation
recommendation.body: First land a session-isolated durable ledger and reliable transcript lifecycle with real client proof, then review context packs and policy configuration separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The commit history ties the core Talk provider, protocol, configuration, and client-session architecture most strongly to this owner.
